proposals.before: The imperial edict read: "Among King Wen's ten sons, Kang Shu alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
proposals.after: The imperial edict read: "Kang Shu had ten kinsmen, and he alone was honored, because this was to reward virtue.
proposals.reason: Chinese 康叔親屬有十而獨尊者 does not name King Wen; the idiomatic rendering invents that referent.

proposals.before: In the third month of year 6, day wu-shen first day, day yi-hai, Censor subject Guang acting as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and Aide Fei, sent the censor memorial, saying: Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Grand Herald subject Xi, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, risking death submit: Grand Marshal Qubing submitted memorial saying: 'Your Majesty has favored me excessively, allowing subject Qubing to await punishment in the ranks of the honored.
proposals.after: In the third month of year 6, day wu-shen first day, day yi-hai, Censor subject Guang acting as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat and Aide Fei, sent the censor memorial, saying: Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Grand Herald subject Xi, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan, risking death submit: Grand Marshal Qubing submitted memorial saying: 'Your Majesty has favored me excessively, allowing subject Qubing to await punishment in the ranks of the honored.
proposals.reason: 青翟 is Qing Di; literal Qing Que is a clear name mistranscription.

proposals.before: Subjects Qing Que, Tang and others should uphold righteousness and follow duty, foolishly dull and not up to affairs.
proposals.after: Subjects Qing Di, Tang and others should uphold righteousness and follow duty, foolishly dull and not up to affairs.
proposals.reason: Same 青翟 mistranscribed as Qing Que in the literal field.

proposals.before: 'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects respectfully with Marquis subject Ying Qi, central two thousand shi and two thousand shi subject He, Remonstrance Official and Erudite subject An and others discuss: We have heard that Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred, the Ji surname stood together, supporting the Son of Heaven.
proposals.after: 'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects respectfully with Marquis subject Ying Qi, central two thousand shi and two thousand shi subject He, Remonstrance Official and Erudite subject An and others discuss: We have heard that Zhou enfeoffed eight hundred, the Ji surname stood together, supporting the Son of Heaven.
proposals.reason: 青翟 again mistranscribed as Qing Que in the literal English.

proposals.before: Continues the line of Xiao Wen Zhong at Ju, rewards and encourages ministers like Pingjin Marquis and others.
proposals.after: Continues the line of Xiao Wen Zhong at Zan, rewards and encourages ministers like Pingjin Marquis and others.
proposals.reason: Place name 酂 is Zan, not Ju; the literal mistranslates the toponym.

proposals.before: 'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects Qing Que and others with marquises, officials of two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others discuss: Risking death memorialize requesting to establish imperial sons as feudal kings.
proposals.after: 'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Censor-in-Chief subject Tang risking death speak: Subjects Qing Di and others with marquises, officials of two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others discuss: Risking death memorialize requesting to establish imperial sons as feudal kings.
proposals.reason: 青翟 is Qing Di; literal wrongly romanizes 翟 as Que.

proposals.before: The imperial edict read: 'Among King Wen's ten sons, Kang Shu alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
proposals.after: The imperial edict read: 'Among Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, he alone was singled out for honor because he was recognized for his virtue.
proposals.reason: Chinese 康叔親屬有十而獨尊者 does not name King Wen; idiomatic invents King Wen.

proposals.before: Subjects Qing Que, Tang, Erudite subject Jiang Xing and others have heard that Kang Shu had ten relatives, King Wu succeeded to the throne, Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, eight of them were established as great states by the honor of their ancestors.
proposals.after: Subjects Qing Di, Tang, Erudite subject Jiang Xing and others have heard that Kang Shu had ten relatives, King Wu succeeded to the throne, Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, eight of them were established as great states by the honor of their ancestors.
proposals.reason: Same 青翟/Qing Di romanization error in the literal.

proposals.before: Now feudal lords' branch sons are enfeoffed as feudal kings, yet to make imperial sons marquises, subjects Qing Que, Tang and others secretly and prostrate consider it, all think noble and base lose order, causing the world to lose hope, cannot.
proposals.after: Now feudal lords' branch sons are enfeoffed as feudal kings, yet to make imperial sons marquises, subjects Qing Di, Tang and others secretly and prostrate consider it, all think noble and base lose order, causing the world to lose hope, cannot.
proposals.reason: Literal misreads 青翟 as Qing Que.

proposals.before: "The Chancellor Qing Di, the Grand Coachman He, the Grand Master of Ceremonies Chong acting as Grandee Secretary, and the Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince An acting as Director of the Imperial Clan, at the risk of death state: We, your servants Qing Di and the others, previously submitted a memorial regarding the Grand Marshal Qubing's petition stating that the imperial princes have not yet been granted titles. We respectfully, together with the Grandee Secretary Tang, the officials of the central two-thousand-shi and two-thousand-shi ranks, the Remonstrant Officials, and the Erudites including Qing, at the risk of death requested that the imperial princes Hong and the others be established as feudal kings.
proposals.after: "The Chancellor Qing Di, the Grand Coachman He, the Grand Master of Ceremonies Chong acting as Grandee Secretary, and An, the Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, acting as Director of the Imperial Clan, at the risk of death state: We, your servants Qing Di and the others, previously submitted a memorial regarding the Grand Marshal Qubing's petition stating that the imperial princes have not yet been granted titles. We respectfully, together with the Grandee Secretary Tang, the officials of the central two-thousand-shi and two-thousand-shi ranks, the Remonstrant Officials, and the Erudites including Qing, at the risk of death requested that the imperial princes Hong and the others be established as feudal kings.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太子少傅臣安 names official An; English wrongly suggests a Crown Prince named An.

proposals.before: 'Chancellor subject Qing Que, Grand Coachman subject He, acting as Censor-in-Chief Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan risking death speak: Subjects Qing Que and others previously memorialized Grand Marshal subject Qubing submitted memorial saying imperial sons have no titles, subjects respectfully with Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, central two thousand shi, two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others risking death request to establish imperial sons subject Hong and others as feudal kings.
proposals.after: 'Chancellor subject Qing Di, Grand Coachman subject He, acting as Censor-in-Chief Grand Master of Ceremonies subject Chong, Crown Prince Junior Tutor subject An acting as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan risking death speak: Subjects Qing Di and others previously memorialized Grand Marshal subject Qubing submitted memorial saying imperial sons have no titles, subjects respectfully with Censor-in-Chief subject Tang, central two thousand shi, two thousand shi, remonstrance officials, erudites subject Qing and others risking death request to establish imperial sons subject Hong and others as feudal kings.
proposals.reason: Literal misromanizes 青翟 as Qing Que.

proposals.before: Subjects Qing Que and others secretly with Marquis subject Shou Cheng and twenty-seven others discuss; all said this violates the proper order of high and low.
proposals.after: Subjects Qing Di and others secretly with Marquis subject Shou Cheng and twenty-seven others discuss; all said this violates the proper order of high and low.
proposals.reason: Literal misromanizes 青翟 as Qing Que.

proposals.before: The Xiongnu are cruel and beastly by nature, invading and plundering as bandits and thieves, and moreover they deal treacherously with the border settlements.
proposals.after: The Xiongnu are cruel to the aged and beast-hearted, invading and plundering as bandits and thieves, and moreover they deal treacherously with the border settlements.
proposals.reason: Chinese 虐老獸心 specifically includes cruelty to the aged (虐老); the idiomatic rendering drops that element and flattens it to generic beastliness.

proposals.before: I commanded generals to go punish their crimes, ten thousand man leaders, thousand man leaders, thirty-two lords all came, surrendered and fled the army.
proposals.after: I commanded generals to go punish their crimes; ten-thousand-man leaders, thousand-man leaders, and thirty-two lords all came, surrendering at the appointed time and fleeing to our forces.
proposals.reason: 降期奔師 means they surrendered on schedule and fled toward (joined) the Han forces; literal English wrongly has them flee the army.

proposals.before: What wise rulers make, certainly not what shallow learners can know, not what broad learning strong memory gentlemen cannot thoroughly understand the intent.
proposals.after: What a wise ruler makes is certainly not something shallow learners can know; it is not something that gentlemen of broad learning and strong memory cannot thoroughly fathom in its intent.
proposals.reason: The double negation 非…所不能 is garbled into ungrammatical English that obscures the meaning.

proposals.before: he admonished the King of Yan not to stir up resentment and not to turn from virtue;
proposals.after: he admonished the King of Yan not to stir up resentment and not to cultivate virtue;
proposals.reason: Chinese 無修德 is a prohibition parallel to 無作怨; "not to turn from virtue" reverses the polarity of 無.

proposals.before: warned the King of Yan not to create resentment, not to turn from virtue;
proposals.after: warned the King of Yan not to create resentment, not to cultivate virtue;
proposals.reason: Literal 無修德 means "do not cultivate virtue," not "not to turn from virtue."

proposals.before: Also saying 'ministers do not create awe' means do not let them because of lightness double righteousness.
proposals.after: Also saying 'ministers do not create awe' means do not let them, because of [the people's] lightness, betray righteousness.
proposals.reason: 倍義 means betray righteousness, not "double" it.

proposals.before: Now land and townships increasingly few, I wish to together with King Xu of Guangling raise troops.
proposals.after: Now land and townships increasingly few, I wish to together with the King of Guangling raise troops.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only 廣陵王; the literal invents the personal name Xu.

proposals.before: Establish King Xu of Guangling as supreme, I again rule Chu 32 cities, like King Yuan time.'
proposals.after: Establish the King of Guangling as supreme, I again rule Chu 32 cities, like King Yuan time.'
proposals.reason: Chinese has only ［立］廣陵王; the literal invents the personal name Xu.

proposals.before: 'Do not pity virtue' means do not let king turn back on virtue.
proposals.after: 'Do not go against virtue' means do not let the king turn back on virtue.
proposals.reason: 俷 means to violate or go against, not to pity; the literal mistranslates 無俷德.

decisions.after: The imperial edict read: "Among Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, he alone was singled out for honor because this was to reward virtue.
decisions.reason: 康叔親屬有十而獨尊者 names Kang Shu's ten kinsmen, not King Wen's sons; the proposal rightly drops the invention, but its after is awkward, so revise to keep the clear among-kinsmen wording and 褒有德也 as rewarding virtue.
